dedupe_keys.name: dispatches design integration and synthesis platform to advance tightly coupled hybrid energy systems

description: DISPATCHES is a platform for designing and optimising integrated energy systems, such as existing nuclear or fossil plants hybridised with storage or hydrogen production, for operation within bulk power markets. It is developed within the DOE Grid Modernization Laboratory Consortium, with contributors including Daniel Gunter, Keith Beattie, John Siirola, Alex Dowling, Darice Guittet, Andrew Lee, Jaffer Ghouse and Konor Frick, and was first registered in 2021 through Idaho National Laboratory. Its goal is to find flexible, dynamic designs that respond to day-ahead, real-time and ancillary service market signals obtained from a production cost model, covering hybridised existing plants and greenfield designs with advanced modular reactors or new coal technology, and handling technologies with different time constants. Example notebooks show its features and can run in a temporary cloud environment through Binder. Coverage is not tied to a place. The code is accessible on GitHub under a BSD-style licence held by the software owners (2020 to 2023) at no cost, with documentation on ReadTheDocs and ten tags. Caveats: it depends on a large process modelling stack, and the licence year suggests reduced activity after 2023. Simulation uses are optimising hybrid plant design and market operation. Related records: model-egret provides grid optimisation formulations of the kind used in production cost studies.
